Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Welcome Phase 3 Action Phase 4 Morning Phase 5 Game End Overview Become the richest innkeeper of the land The round is divided into 3 phases: Welcome Phase Action Phase Morning Phase Welcome Phase The first player for the round draws guest cards one at a time and places them in an unlocked unoccupied room of their choice Action Phase In turn order, each player takes 1 action until everyone has taken 2 actions The actions are: Bribe Build Kill Bury Pass The basics of all actions (Aside from Pass) are as follows: Choose a guest Play a number of additional cards defined by the rank of the chosen guest (0-3 on lower left) From all these cards, reclaim all which show the aptitude for the action (Symbol on their name banner) Those not selected are placed into either the Exit stack or the Bistro (Peasants) as appropriate Finally, perform the action itself The actions in detail: Bribe (Money Aptitude) The chosen guest must reside either in an inn room or the Bistro In addition to those with Aptitude, the originally selected guest is also added to your hand (if it didn't already have Aptitude) If you bribed the peasants, you may take 2 instead of 1 Build (Shovel Aptitude) The chosen guest must reside in your hand and contain an Annex (house symbol) on the lower left Place them living side up in front of you Each Annex has a special effect which will trigger upon building it Kill (Gun Aptitude) The chosen guest must reside either in an inn room or the Bistro Place them dead side up in front of you (They are a corpse, but not yet buried, so could pose a risk) Bury (Coffin Aptitude) The chosen guest must reside in front of you dead side up Place the chosen guest under a previously built Annex, yours or someone else's, whilst still being able to see their value Each Annex can hold a number of dead guests equal to its rank (e.g. a rank 2 Annex can hold 2 bodies, but make sure both values are viewable) A rank 0 Annex can therefore NOT hold a dead guest Upon burial, the value of the guest is halved and half goes to you and half goes to the owner of the Annex (which may also be you) You cannot exceed the 40 money total from this Pass (No Aptitude) This doesn't follow the normal action structure, and instead takes the following route: You may exchange Cash for Cheques or Cheques for Cash in denominations of 10 only Cheques have no limit, whilst Cash is limited to the 40 shown on the board Morning Phase This phase is divided into the following three steps: Police Departure Wages On the Police step, if there is a police officer in one of the rooms, any player with a corpse (unburied dead guest) must discard it and pay 10 money (Cash OR Cheque). If you have more than one unburied corpse, you must do this for each one, i.e. 2 unburied corpses would cost 20 money and you'd lose both. If you cannot afford the total sum, pay to 0 then the rest is ignored On the Departure step, earn 1 money for guests still in the rooms you own, then all the guests get moved to the Exit stack On the Wages step, pay 1 money for each card in your hand, these ONLY accept Cash. If you cannot pay for all your cards, choose which unpaid ones to discard Finally, the first player marker moves on Game End The game ends the second time the entrance stack empties. If the inn is able to be filled as normal, complete the final round, if you can't fill all rooms required, the game ends before that round. Each player with an unburied corpse must pay 10 money (Cash or Cheque) and discard the guest Check if you have any Rank 3 Annexes which earn you Cash money (Again you cannot go over 40) The player with the most wealth (Cash + Cheques) is the winner. If there's a tie, the winner is the tie

[Rating: 1/10] PRO: extravagant theme and visuals over a run off the mill multi-purpose card based engine building euro. CON: see above.   On one level there's this interesting theme with a bit different visuals (from artists of Brazilian Coup) that could have worked a bit more on legibility of fonts. On the other level's it's same old optimising game with restricted actions and a chain of resource conversion (to get money you need to: get cards in your hand, build a new building, kill a guest, bury it under a building. For each of these you pay with cards). The there's a whole lot of restrictions and most o

[Rating: 1/10] I think making a game where players have to effectively kill innocent sleeping people, just for getting points, is highly disturbing and irritating.  For me there is a big difference between killing/defending against evil enemies and killing innocent people while they are sleeping like you have to do it in this game.  Probably their next expansion will be poisoning newborn babies for victory points while they are sleeping.  Don't get it why people are even playing this game.  Extremely annoying.

[Rating: 1/10] A game of running an inn, killing and burying your guests to steal their money. It's an engine building game where you recruit people or expand your inn to make yourself more efficient, which makes it a "meh" game to me. The nice mechanic of burying a body under someone else's inn and split the money 50:50 is interesting, but it wasn't enough interaction to me to make me want to play the game.  After a few repeated game of it, I am done with it.

[Rating: 2/10] Nice theme, easy to learn. But there should be 3 actions, with 2 you can do almost nothing.  Just too slow, not much you can do in one turn so you need too much turns and still it falls flat then.

[Rating: 2/10] There’s nothing to redeem in this dry, uninspiringly Bloody Inn: it’s an eurogame of the worst kind, one of those that take a sick pleasure in preventing you from doing what actions you need whenever you need them done but force you to be content with the little you can take out of their oppressive rules.

[Rating: 2/10] Yeah, as suspected and warned. The theme is great. The art is great. The gameplay is eh. Just a puzzle - get cards into your hand, play the number, get a couple of cards in front of you to do a thing. Most of it is that, so the actual murder of guests is far from remarkable or chilling, it's just getting some VP.   Even the kids see straight through it which is a sign of what it misses.

[Rating: 2/10] Still trying to figure out if this game is a keeper. But it scratches a similar San Juan itch - and I'd rather play San Juan.

[Rating: 2.5/10] Some of the least interesting decisions for one of the most unnecessarily clunky and slow moving games. I also don't understand how the card powers were the most boring things they could come up with. End game scoring opportunities? Psh no, how about earn one extra coin a turn instead (or MAYBE one extra coin, ooooooooo). Just a monumental flop of a game.

[Rating: 2.8/10] I loathed this 'game'.  This is such a failure of playtesting, I'm not sure the word 'game' really applies.  I think the theme is good, and the concepts are there, but the mechanics are an absolute failure.  The two actions per round is restrictive that it is in such diametric contrast to the rest of the game.  Is it an engine game?  No...none of the cards do anything really interesting, and even if they did, the game will reset before you can even determine a non-frustrating plan of action. [Rating: 3/10] I had high hopes for it... In fact it offers too few actions, only two in a round. THat's not enaugh for what you are planning for. It takes too long until you get your engine to work. And this is point 2. After you got you hand to a certain point, you wont change it a lot and it will be allways the same. This one was one of two must-buys and now is the only disappointment of Essen.  - purchased Spiel15 - sold 01.11.2015 (BGG Store); 15€

[Rating: 3/10] Yikes, this was one of the worst games I played that year - and it's one I am pretty sure I will never play again! Which is a bit odd since lots of people like it, but I did not enjoy it at all! The game mechanics didn't mesh well nor resonate with me, the art was awful and the theme was weird.
